title: Why you think you're above average, even when you're not
hook: Why do most people believe they are better than average drivers?

narration.text: Most people rate their own abilities as above average, even in areas like intelligence or humour.
This cognitive bias is called the Dunning-Kruger effect.
People with low competence often lack the self-awareness to recognise their own mistakes.
Their limited knowledge prevents them from seeing how much they don't know.
Conversely, highly skilled people often underestimate their own abilities, assuming tasks are easy for everyone.
Recognising this effect can help us be more open to learning and improving.
It encourages us to seek feedback and challenge our assumptions.
Have you noticed this overconfidence in yourself or others?

description: Have you ever wondered why nearly everyone thinks they are above average? It's not just ego; it's a fascinating cognitive bias. This video explains the Dunning-Kruger effect and how it shapes our self-perception.
topic: Why people tend to rate themselves as above average in many abilities, explaining the Dunning-Kruger effect.
